requirements.packages_why: OLMo-Hybrid is a GATED DELTA NET (linear attention), NOT a Mamba hybrid, so its kernels come from `fla` and NOT from mamba-ssm / causal-conv1d. Without it `is_flash_linear_attention_available()` is False and transformers SILENTLY substitutes torch_chunk_gated_delta_rule / torch_recurrent_gated_delta_rule -- pure-PyTorch recurrences -- with no warning in any log. Measured on that fallback 2026-08-20: 19.0 s/cell on an A100 (GPU 6% busy, process at 2545% CPU) and 19.10 s/cell on MPS. IDENTICAL on both devices, which is the signature of a path that never properly reaches either accelerator, and it cost ~2 h of A100 time plus most of a day of MPS before the cause was found. **THE `ssm` PROFILE DOES NOT COVER THIS.** It installs mamba-ssm + causal-conv1d and its description says 'SSM and hybrid', but `hybrid` there means Falcon-H1 (Mamba2 + attention) whose measured 19.3x says nothing about this architecture. Both mamba kernels imported cleanly on the box where this ran slow -- which is exactly why checking them came back fine and sent the search elsewhere. Assert the boolean instead: `transformers.models.olmo_hybrid.modeling_olmo_hybrid.is_fast_path_available`. CUDA-ONLY, and declared anyway: every fla backend extra requires triton and there is no Metal build, so this cannot accelerate the model on the Mac at any version -- Olmo-Hybrid is a CLOUD-ONLY lineage for speed. Installing it here is harmless because that availability check gates on `is_torch_cuda_available()` first, so it stays False on MPS rather than promising a fast path that is not there. The archive knew this from the other side: data/cloud_profiles.json in ~/github/malign-logits carries a `vllm_nightly` profile noted 'For allenai/Olmo-Hybrid ONLY', because vLLM 0.27.1 raised TypeError at olmo_gdn_linear_attn.py:517 -- the same architecture, named in the path.

gated delta net kernels; same architecture as the base arm, see allenai/Olmo-Hybrid-7B for the measurement and why the `ssm` profile does not supply them. Without fla this arm runs the pure-PyTorch fallback at ~19 s/cell on every device.

requirements.packages_why: Baichuan2's bundled modelling code imports bitsandbytes and transformers refuses the load without it. INVISIBLE FROM THIS MACHINE: the Mac has no CUDA, so bitsandbytes cannot be installed here at all and the model is simply unmeasurable locally -- the dependency exists only where the work happens. Found 2026-08-20 when both arms died on a rented box after their lineage had otherwise finished; installing it recovered 5,227 pass-2 cells.

requirements.transformers_reason: compute in bfloat16, NOT float16: fp16 overflows the SSM scan and yields all-NaN logits on prompts >=13 tokens (1/12 finite at fp16, 12/12 at bf16). Storage stays f16.

requirements.packages_why: einops: internlm2's BUNDLED modelling_internlm2.py imports it through trust_remote_code, so transformers' check_imports refuses the load before a weight is read. Cost three boxes' worth of diagnosis on 2026-08-20 because the runner truncated the message at exactly the package list. The modelling file ALSO imports flash_attn, and that one is NOT required: this Mac has einops without flash_attn and loads internlm2 fine, so the import is guarded. Declaring flash_attn here would buy a 25-minute compile per box for nothing.
